series.premise: Eighteen years after the ocean turned to glass, fifteen-year-old salvage skater Nila Varma hears her drowned brother calling from beneath the transparent surface.
series.season_engine: Each fracture opens one buried sea-memory and one survival consequence for the coast, revealing who froze the ocean and why it may not survive a sudden release.
series.ending_promise: Nila must free the living sea without drowning the civilization built on its prison.
series.global_image_style: Vertical 9:16 premium cute cinematic 3D feature-animation, original compact stylized characters with large expressive eyes, vast translucent glass ocean, coral light beneath the surface, wind-swept South Asian coastal settlements, tactile cloth, salt and crystal, mythic scale with emotionally truthful acting; preserve locked character sheets exactly; no graphic harm.

characters.name: Nila Varma
characters.lock: small dark-brown-skinned Indian teen girl, huge sea-green eyes, oval face, wind-tangled black hair in two short braids, coral-red sailcloth jacket, teal tunic, charcoal trousers, silver blade-skates, shell compass at throat
characters.acting: physical confidence masks grief; pauses to read risk before committing

characters.name: Tavi
characters.lock: tiny brown-skinned Indian boy, round face, large amber eyes, fluffy black curls, oversized sky-blue goggles, cream poncho, mustard shorts over leggings, green boots, folding kite-map backpack
characters.acting: turns fear into questions; corrects adults without performing cleverness

characters.name: Oru
characters.role: young sea-spirit separated from the trapped ocean
characters.lock: cute otter-sized translucent water creature, rounded fins, two luminous cyan eyes, coral-pink glow at heart, flowing tail suspended inside a clear droplet body, no mouth
characters.acting: emotion through water shape, bubbles and heart-light; never pet-like

characters.name: Arun Varma
characters.role: Nila's older brother preserved beneath the glass
characters.lock: Indian young man age twenty-two, deep brown skin, gentle green-brown eyes, wavy black hair floating underwater, faded saffron rescue vest, navy shirt, shell bracelet matching Nila
characters.acting: protective without directing Nila's choices; carries eighteen years of isolation

characters.name: Captain Mira Varma
characters.role: Nila's mother and leader of the surface caravans
characters.lock: strong Indian woman early forties, dark brown skin, sharp sea-green eyes, long black braid threaded with white shell beads, indigo captain coat, rust sash, crystal-hook staff
characters.acting: decisive survival logic with visible maternal conflict

characters.name: Admiral Soren
characters.role: guardian of the Freeze Engine and ruler of the glass routes
characters.lock: tall Indian man late forties, bronze-brown skin, pale grey eyes, close-cropped salt hair, white-and-navy crystal armor, long storm cape, black glass spear
characters.acting: formal restraint; genuinely fears the thaw more than loss of power

characters.name: Mahi
characters.role: ancient human voice chosen by the living ocean
characters.lock: ageless brown-skinned woman, luminous turquoise eyes, very long silver-blue hair moving like waves, layered pearl-grey sari formed from water ribbons, bare feet above the surface
characters.acting: speaks as one person carrying many perspectives, never vague prophecy

characters.name: Lio Soren
characters.role: Soren's adult daughter and elected leader of a deep settlement
characters.lock: brown-skinned Indian woman age twenty-seven, steady pale-grey eyes matching Soren, cropped black curls, turquoise deep-water suit beneath woven white shawl, coral breathing collar, childhood silver bracelet carried at belt
characters.acting: affection without surrendering authority; corrects surface assumptions directly

characters.name: Professor Kala Varma
characters.role: inventor suspended inside the Freeze Engine and Nila's grandmother
characters.lock: elderly dark-brown-skinned Indian woman, bright sea-green eyes, long white braid floating around face, copper engineering suit beneath translucent frost mantle, crystalline heartbeat harness across chest
characters.acting: curious and exact despite exhaustion; refuses automatic moral authority

episodes.title: Her Brother Knocked Beneath the Sea
episodes.logline: Nila hears Arun beneath a surface frozen for eighteen years.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila confirms Arun survives and creates the first fracture.
episodes.location: moonlit glass ocean near Varma Harbor
beats: Nila skates over black water locked beneath clear glass.
Three knocks answer the shell compass she inherited from Arun.
Tavi maps a warm shape moving far below them.
Nila cuts the forbidden surface despite patrol warnings.
A single living droplet leaps out and becomes Oru.
Oru projects Arun trapped inside a coral-lit air pocket.
Nila promises rescue without knowing the glass supports their entire city.
The hairline crack races toward Varma Harbor faster than they can skate.

episodes.title: The Crack Reached the Harbor
episodes.logline: A rescue fracture threatens homes anchored to the frozen sea.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila seals the immediate breach and accepts responsibility publicly.
episodes.location: Varma Harbor built on glass pylons
beats: The crack splits beneath market houses as trapped waves push upward.
Captain Mira orders everyone to blame an old pressure fault.
Nila admits she opened the sea to reach Arun.
Citizens demand Oru be returned before the glass collapses.
Oru shows the fracture can close only with freely released surface water.
Families donate drinking water despite the coming dry season.
The seal holds, proving the ocean responds to voluntary exchange.
Admiral Soren arrives carrying a warrant for Nila and her mother.

episodes.title: The Admiral Knew Arun Was Alive
episodes.logline: Soren reveals he has monitored survivors beneath the glass for years.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila learns hundreds may survive below and escapes official custody.
episodes.location: crystal patrol ship skating toward the capital
beats: Soren arrests Nila but protects Oru from frightened soldiers.
His charts show human heartbeats beneath seven deep-sea shelters.
He hid them because opening one route could drown millions above.
Mira admits she knew Arun's signal continued for one year.
Nila rejects both adults deciding grief was safer than truth.
Tavi folds the official chart into a wind kite.
Oru pulls their prison sled through a temporary water lane.
The stolen chart marks Arun's shelter directly beneath the Freeze Engine.

episodes.title: Her Mother Chose the Surface
episodes.logline: Mira explains the night she sealed Arun beneath the sea.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila understands Mira's choice but refuses continued secrecy.
episodes.location: memory storm on the glass flats
beats: Oru releases a salt memory of the ocean's final moving night.
A tsunami approached while the experimental Freeze Engine failed.
Arun stayed below to close one flooded shelter gate.
Mira activated the engine before he could surface.
The freeze saved coastal cities and trapped every swimmer below.
Mira chose millions over Arun but then concealed the survivors.
Nila distinguishes the emergency choice from eighteen years of silence.
The memory ends with Arun sabotaging the engine from underneath.

episodes.title: Arun Was Breaking the Ocean Free
episodes.logline: Arun's sabotage forces Nila to question whether rescue can wait.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila establishes contact and a deadline of thirty tides.
episodes.location: thin-glass listening well
beats: Tavi builds a listening well above Arun's shelter.
Arun speaks through vibrations rather than magical prophecy.
He says oxygen systems will fail after thirty lunar tides.
His fractures were distress signals, not a plan to flood cities.
Nila asks him to pause sabotage while she finds a controlled thaw.
Arun agrees only if surface citizens learn the truth now.
Nila broadcasts his heartbeat through harbor bells.
Soren shuts every route and activates a second Freeze Engine.

episodes.title: The Second Engine Froze Memory
episodes.logline: Soren's backup machine makes citizens forget the ocean was ever liquid.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Tavi preserves pre-freeze history in physical maps.
episodes.location: capital glassway under white freezing light
beats: White light spreads from the capital across the glass.
Citizens call the transparent surface ordinary crystal land.
Mira forgets ships, tides and Arun's rescue service.
Tavi's paper kite-maps resist the engine's field.
Nila uses them to re-teach one concrete memory at a time.
Soren says forgetting prevents mass panic and reckless drilling.
Oru absorbs the field long enough for Nila to reach the controls.
The overloaded spirit begins freezing completely solid from its heart outward.

episodes.title: Oru Turned to Glass
episodes.logline: Saving Oru requires returning a memory Nila prefers to keep.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila gives up sole ownership of her final memory with Arun.
episodes.location: abandoned tide temple
beats: Oru's clear body hardens while its coral heart flickers.
The tide temple asks for a living memory of moving water.
Nila holds the last morning she and Arun sailed together.
Using it will let Oru carry the memory independently.
Nila shares rather than erases it, accepting altered ownership.
Oru liquefies and projects the sailing memory from its perspective.
Tavi notices a second child hidden aboard Arun's old boat.
The child is Soren's daughter, officially dead since the Freeze.

episodes.title: The Admiral's Daughter Lived Below
episodes.logline: Soren's personal loss exposes why he protects the prison he hates.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Soren agrees to a secret inspection beneath the surface.
episodes.location: Soren's sealed memorial pavilion
beats: Nila brings the recovered boat memory to Soren during the cold predawn watch before the storm.
He recognizes nine-year-old Lio entering Arun's shelter.
Soren believed she died before activating the engine.
He refuses hope until Oru reproduces her current heartbeat.
Nila offers no forgiveness bargain, only verified evidence.
Soren grants one descent through a maintenance shaft.
He keeps the engine active to prevent uncontrolled thaw.
The shaft opens, and warm seawater rises instead of falling.

episodes.title: They Walked Under the Ocean
episodes.logline: Nila enters the inverted world sustained beneath the frozen sea.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The surface team reaches the submerged settlements.
episodes.location: air tunnel beneath the glass ocean
beats: A crystal stair descends into an air tunnel under crushing water.
Fish swim above them against the glass ceiling.
Oru leads them through coral grown around abandoned trains.
Soren sees shelters his charts reduced to numbers.
Tavi finds children born below who have never seen rain.
Nila reaches Arun but respects the quarantine door between them.
Arun looks older than Mira and younger than his own voice.
Behind him, the shelter wall splits and the living ocean speaks Nila's name.

episodes.title: The Ocean Asked for a Body
episodes.logline: The living sea chooses Nila as its messenger, threatening her individual voice.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Mahi manifests separately after Nila refuses possession.
episodes.location: Arun's failing deep shelter
beats: Warm water forms words directly inside Nila's breath.
The ocean asks to use her body to negotiate with the surface.
Arun says earlier messengers lost their identities in the collective.
Soren wants the contact severed before it controls the thaw.
Nila offers the shell compass as a temporary voice instead.
The ocean accepts her boundary and fills the shell with light.
Mahi emerges as a separate water-formed person.
She announces the sea itself has only twenty tides left to live.

episodes.title: The Sea Was Dying in Its Prison
episodes.logline: Mahi reveals the Freeze preserved humans while suffocating ocean circulation.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Surface and below settlements accept a shared twenty-tide deadline.
episodes.location: coral council chamber below the glass
beats: Dead currents have created rapidly expanding lifeless dark zones beneath the ancient glass.
Below settlers need the ceiling; sea life needs circulation.
Soren proposes thawing only uninhabited ocean sectors.
Mahi explains currents cannot be divided by political maps.
Arun demands immediate truth for both populations.
Nila organizes a council with equal seats for surface, below and Mahi.
They agree to test one reversible current channel.
The chosen channel runs through the capital's only freshwater reservoir.

episodes.title: Fresh Water or Living Sea
episodes.logline: The first current test risks contaminating the surface's drinking supply.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The capital accepts rationing to permit a controlled ocean current.
episodes.location: freshwater reservoir above a trapped current
beats: A blue current presses beneath the capital reservoir.
Opening it will add salt and cut drinking water for weeks.
Mira argues the harbor poor cannot absorb another ration.
Mahi refuses to let sea life remain the invisible sacrifice.
Tavi maps rain collectors that wealthy towers kept private.
Citizens release stored rainwater before voting on the channel.
Nila opens a narrow current and monitors both salt and pressure.
The sea moves safely, but something enormous wakes inside the dark zone.

episodes.title: A City-Sized Whale Woke Below
episodes.logline: An ancient whale carries the Freeze Engine's missing counter-song.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The whale joins the thaw but its movement destabilizes three settlements.
episodes.location: deep dark zone beneath the capital
beats: A luminous whale unfolds from eighteen years of stillness.
Its first heartbeat cracks glass across three inhabited sectors.
Arun wants it sedated until evacuations finish.
Mahi says another forced sleep could kill the last migration memory.
Nila uses Oru's water pulses to ask the whale to wait.
It agrees for one tide after hearing the settlements' signals.
Its song reveals the engine was designed for seven days, not eighteen years.
Mira admits surface leaders removed every automatic thaw command.

episodes.title: The Freeze Was Never Meant to Last
episodes.logline: Mira faces evidence that leaders extended the emergency to protect their new power.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Mira releases the original engine records publicly.
episodes.location: surface caravan command ship
beats: Original plans schedule a gradual thaw seven days after the tsunami.
Caravan founders disabled it once glass trade made them wealthy.
Mira inherited the secret and believed reversal had become too dangerous.
Nila accuses her of turning a hard emergency into permanent policy.
Soren offers to share blame if the records stay sealed until evacuation.
Mira refuses another strategic silence and broadcasts everything.
Surface workers begin strikes against crystal extraction.
The capital council orders Nila's entire family exiled onto unstable outer glass.

episodes.title: Exile Crossed the Singing Crack
episodes.logline: The exiled caravan discovers cracks can carry safe currents when people move with them.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila develops mobile thaw routes instead of fixed breaches.
episodes.location: outer glass during a singing storm
beats: Wind turns branching fractures into a terrifying musical chord.
The caravan cannot stop because weight concentrated in one place will break through.
Tavi maps the chord as pressure moving beneath their skates.
Mahi teaches Oru to answer with a slower current rhythm.
Nila guides everyone along the moving safe line instead of away from every crack.
Mira trusts Nila's route despite losing command authority.
A mobile channel circulates water without collapsing the surface.
The song attracts Lio, Soren's daughter, riding a living wave from below.

episodes.title: Lio Refused to Return Home
episodes.logline: Soren's daughter rejects rescue defined as returning to the surface.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Soren recognizes below-born society as a home, not a waiting room.
episodes.location: outer-glass meeting camp
beats: Lio embraces Soren but says she came to negotiate, not be rescued.
She has a family and leadership role in the deep settlements.
Soren calls eighteen years below stolen childhood.
Lio says his grief cannot decide where her adult life belongs.
Nila asks both to speak without making reunion conditional.
Soren returns Lio's childhood bracelet without asking her to wear it.
They agree to know each other across two homes.
Lio reveals Arun has been hiding a device capable of shattering the entire ocean.

episodes.title: Arun Built the Shatter Key
episodes.logline: Arun's emergency weapon divides survivors who are running out of air.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Arun surrenders sole control of the Shatter Key.
episodes.location: deep shelter engineering bay
beats: The Shatter Key could collapse the glass into safe-sized plates within minutes.
Its models save most below shelters but destroy unknown surface routes.
Arun built it after unanswered distress calls, not for revenge.
Desperate residents want him to activate it before oxygen fails.
Nila refuses to destroy the device while its need remains real.
Arun places its activation pieces with surface, below and Mahi representatives.
No one side can now shatter the ocean alone.
One piece is stolen before the agreement is announced.

episodes.title: Tavi Stole the Shatter Piece
episodes.logline: Tavi takes the key to stop adults repeating secret decisions, but creates a new secret himself.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Tavi returns the piece and gains an accountable youth seat on the council.
episodes.location: kite tunnels between surface and below
beats: Nila follows Tavi's folding maps into a narrow ventilation shaft.
He stole the piece because every council member once defended a harmful secret.
Tavi plans to hide it where nobody can complete the weapon.
Nila agrees with his distrust but names the power he took alone.
Oru shows children in failing shelters whose survival depends on a backup.
Tavi returns the piece publicly and explains his reasoning.
The council creates a youth seat with access and review rather than symbolic presence.
Tavi's map reveals a natural thaw path directly beneath the original tsunami wall.

episodes.title: The Frozen Tsunami Was Still Moving
episodes.logline: The disaster paused eighteen years ago will resume when the ocean thaws.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The coast begins preparing to face the original wave rather than refreeze it.
episodes.location: vertical glass wall at the edge of the ocean
beats: The expedition reaches a mountain of glass shaped like a breaking wave.
Inside, fish and wreckage still move by fractions of a millimeter.
Soren proposes redirecting all thaw energy to keep the wave frozen forever.
Mahi says the trapped pressure is poisoning every current.
Mira identifies abandoned inland channels designed before leaders chose coastal wealth.
Communities vote to relocate despite losing homes built on glass trade.
Nila opens one drainage channel and the wave moves one safe meter.
The shift exposes the Freeze Engine's heart inside the wave itself.

episodes.title: The Engine Had a Human Heart
episodes.logline: The Freeze Engine is powered by the suspended consciousness of its inventor.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Professor Varma awakens and rejects indefinite use of her sacrifice.
episodes.location: engine chamber inside the frozen tsunami
beats: A woman sleeps within the engine, every heartbeat sending cold across the sea.
Mira identifies her mother, Professor Kala Varma, believed killed during activation.
Kala chose seven days of suspension and never consented to eighteen years.
Mira argues waking her now could restart the tsunami.
Nila opens a communication path without interrupting the heart rhythm.
Kala asks them to finish the evacuation and end the engine.
Arun forgives no one but commits his engineering to a controlled shutdown.
Kala warns the engine will fail by itself in ten tides, not twenty.

episodes.title: Ten Tides to Move a Civilization
episodes.logline: Surface and below populations must relocate through the same limited corridors.
episodes.permanent_story_change: A shared evacuation replaces competing rescue plans.
episodes.location: coastal evacuation map spanning both worlds
beats: Every safe corridor can carry surface caravans or below shelters, not both at once.
Old leaders prioritize whoever their maps already count.
Tavi overlays heartbeats, homes, disabilities and current speeds on one living map.
Lio proposes staggered movement paired across surface and below communities.
Nila rejects lotteries that hide political choices behind chance.
Public councils publish reasons and allow appeals for each route.
The first paired evacuation succeeds without a priority class.
A crystal storm destroys the remaining nine planned corridors.

episodes.title: Only Oru Could Carry the Map
episodes.logline: Oru must hold the changing evacuation network, risking dissolution into the ocean.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Oru shares the map across many water-bearers instead of becoming one central system.
episodes.location: crystal storm over broken corridors
beats: Paper, crystal and radio maps fail as every route shifts.
Oru can feel all connected water and could guide everyone simultaneously.
Mahi warns total connection may dissolve Oru's separate identity.
Oru initially volunteers because being useful feels like its purpose.
Nila asks for a design that includes Oru's right to disconnect.
Tavi distributes small water lenses to thousands of local navigators.
Oru shares updates without holding every traveler inside itself.
The network finds one route through the moving frozen tsunami.

episodes.title: The Wave Remembered Every Ship
episodes.logline: Thawing memory-wrecks block the final route with unresolved distress signals.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Families receive truth about lost sailors without treating wrecks as salvage.
episodes.location: memory current inside the tsunami
beats: Ghostlike images of ships repeat their final calls inside the wave.
Surface salvagers race to claim cargo before the thaw destroys it.
Mira recognizes orders she gave captains moments before freezing them.
Nila stops her from sinking with the wrecks as private penance.
Families choose which recordings to receive and which to leave private.
Salvagers clear only physical hazards under community supervision.
The memory current opens a navigable channel.
At its center floats Nila's childhood boat, carrying a second version of Arun.

episodes.title: Two Aruns Reached the Surface
episodes.logline: A sea-memory copy challenges the assumption that only the physical survivor belongs to Nila.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Memory-Arun gains independent recognition without replacing living Arun.
episodes.location: evacuation camp beside the memory current
beats: One Arun climbs from below while another steps from the preserved boat.
Memory-Arun is the nineteen-year-old Nila remembers; living Arun is twenty-two after years beneath.
Mira reaches toward the easier son who has not learned her betrayal.
Living Arun refuses a contest for authenticity.
Mahi confirms the copy can form new choices beyond its stored voyage.
Nila meets both without claiming either as the brother she is owed.
Memory-Arun chooses a new name and joins the water-bearer network.
The engine begins its final uncommanded shutdown three tides early.

episodes.title: The Ocean Cracked Everywhere
episodes.logline: Premature shutdown turns every evacuation into a simultaneous crisis.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The Shatter Key becomes a precision tool rather than a weapon.
episodes.location: entire glass ocean during global fracture
beats: Millions of fractures flash coral-red beneath skaters and settlements.
The three Shatter Key holders can create safe plates but only together.
Panic separates surface, below and Mahi representatives.
Nila uses the distributed water map to reconnect them without central command.
Arun rewrites the key for corridor-sized cuts.
All three authorize one reversible fracture at a time.
Cities float on controlled plates while currents resume between them.
The frozen tsunami finally begins falling toward the evacuated coast.

episodes.title: They Let the Tsunami Fall
episodes.logline: The coast faces the original wave through preparation instead of another freeze.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The eighteen-year emergency ends and the ocean moves again.
episodes.location: evacuated coast and inland drainage valleys
beats: The glass wave liquefies higher than every former tower.
Kala's engine heart slows while citizens shelter along restored inland channels.
Soren wants one last freeze when a barrier fails.
Lio reminds him that fear does not cancel the plan everyone chose.
Nila, Arun and Mahi redirect the wave through multiple open valleys.
Mira commands no one; she carries children beside former deck workers.
The wave crosses empty coast and loses force across wetlands.
For the first time in eighteen years, a natural tide reaches shore.

episodes.title: Nila Could No Longer Skate Home
episodes.logline: The successful thaw destroys Nila's familiar routes and identity as a glass skater.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nila grieves the surface world without treating its loss as proof the thaw was wrong.
episodes.location: open water where Varma Harbor once stood
beats: Nila's blade-skates sink when she steps onto moving water.
Her home survives only as boats tied around former glass pylons.
Celebrations make her ashamed to mourn a necessary change.
Mira admits relief and grief can occupy the same rescue.
Tavi turns Nila's skates into rudders instead of museum objects.
Nila learns to sail badly and accepts being a beginner.
Oru chooses to travel between sea and shore rather than merge with Mahi.
A deep tremor reveals the returning ocean has forgotten how to make storms safely.

episodes.title: The First Storm Had No Memory
episodes.logline: Eighteen years without circulation leaves the ocean unable to regulate its own weather.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Human and ocean communities establish a temporary cooperative weather system.
episodes.location: new open sea beneath a rapidly forming cyclone
beats: A cyclone spins in minutes because heat has nowhere familiar to travel.
Mahi cannot command the ocean; she only carries its many signals.
Soren offers former Freeze Engine mirrors for targeted cooling.
Nila refuses permanent climate control but accepts transparent emergency use.
Tavi's water-lens network maps currents with sailors and sea creatures together.
Arun redirects mirrors while Oru maintains exit signals for marine life.
The storm weakens naturally once circulation paths reconnect.
Kala's heart stops inside the dead engine, and Mira has seconds to wake her.

episodes.title: Kala Chose an Ordinary Life
episodes.logline: The inventor survives but refuses to become the permanent expert ruling the new sea.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Kala joins public accountability and destroys the engine's control core.
episodes.location: silent Freeze Engine chamber at sunrise
beats: Mira opens the chamber and Kala breathes without freezing the water.
Leaders immediately ask her to design a safer permanent engine.
Kala refuses to turn survival guilt into lifelong authority.
She testifies how her seven-day consent was extended by institutions and family.
Mira accepts scrutiny as both daughter and captain.
Kala removes the unique control crystal and divides its harmless records publicly.
Mahi confirms the ocean now holds no human command pathway.
Nila carries the last crystal shard toward the deepest returning current.

episodes.title: The Ocean Moved Beneath Her
episodes.logline: Nila releases the final shard and chooses a future between surface and deep communities.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The sea, survivors and coastal cities live through negotiated shared systems; Nila becomes a route-builder, not a chosen ruler.
episodes.location: open ocean above the former Arun shelter
beats: Nila sails above the shelter where Arun survived eighteen years.
She drops the inert control shard only after Mahi confirms it carries no command.
Below settlements rise in mobile habitats while surface caravans become fleets.
Soren reunites with Lio across two homes rather than bringing her back.
Mira and Arun begin rebuilding a relationship that does not erase their changed ages.
Tavi publishes a living map anyone may correct and nobody owns.
Nila turns her silver skates into the first tools for a sea-and-glass rescue school.
A real wave lifts the boat, and she balances without needing the world to become still.
